accepted.question_text: Let B = ⊕_{n≥0} B_n be a semi-graded ring such that B is left noetherian, B_0 is left noetherian and contained in the center Z(B), each homogeneous piece B_n is finitely generated as a left B_0-module, and B satisfies the χ1 condition. If π : sgr-B → qsgr-B is the quotient from finitely generated semi-graded B-modules to the quotient by torsion modules, s is the degree-shift autoequivalence on qsgr-B, and Γ(π(B))_{≥0} := ⊕_{d≥0} Hom_{qsgr-B}(π(B), s^d(π(B))), does there exist an equivalence of categories qgr-B ≃ qgr-Γ(π(B))_{≥0} extending the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem from finitely graded algebras to semi-graded rings?

evidence.quote: 1.4 Problem 1 • Investigate the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem for semi-graded rings.
Definition 1.21. Let s be the autoequivalence of qsgr − B defined by the shifts of degrees. We define Γ(π(B))≥0 := L∞ d=0 Homqsgr−B(π(B), sd (π(B))).

The solution of Problem 1 is as follows. Theorem 1.24. Let B be a SG ring that satisfies (C1)-(C4) and assume that B satisfies the condition X1, then there exists an equivalence of categories qgr − B ≃ qgr − Γ(π(B))≥0.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a bijective skew PBW extension of an Ore domain R. Does A satisfy a Gelfand-Kirillov type description of its total ring of fractions, meaning that Q(A) is isomorphic to the total ring of fractions of a suitable multiparameter skew quantum polynomial algebra over Q(R), analogous to the quantum Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture? In addition, does taking centers commute with taking total fractions for such algebras, i.e. is Q(Z(A)) isomorphic to Z(Q(A))?
accepted.context_brief: Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew PBW extensions

evidence.quote: The problems that we will analyze and formulate from the general approach of skew P BW extensions and semi-graded rings are: ... 2) Study the Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture ([28]) for bijective skew P BW extensions over Ore domains. Moreover, investigate for them the commutation between the center and the total ring of fractions.
2.1 Problem 2 • Study the Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew P BW extensions over Ore domains. Moreover, investigate for them the isomorphism Q(Z(A)) ∼= Z(Q(A)).

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field and let A = K[x_1, ..., x_n; σ] be the skew polynomial ring in commuting variables satisfying x_i x_j = x_j x_i and x_i r = σ(r) x_i for every r in K, where σ is an automorphism of K of finite order. Give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for A: for every finitely generated projective A-module, explicitly compute a basis. Equivalently, design an algorithm that, given an idempotent matrix F in M_s(A), constructs an invertible matrix U in GL_s(A) such that UFU^{-1} has block form [[0, 0], [0, I_r]], so the final r rows of U form a basis of the projective module generated by the rows of F.
accepted.context_brief: Constructive Quillen-Suslin algorithm for skew polynomial rings

evidence.quote: in [8] was proved that if K is a field, A := K[x1, . . . , xn; σ], σ is an automorphism of K of finite order, xixj = xjxi and xir = σ(r)xi, for every r ∈ K and 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n, then every finitely generated projective module over A is free. The proof in [8] of this theorem (Quillen-Suslin theorem) is not construcitve, i.e., the proof shows the existence of a basis for every finitely generated projective module M over A, but an explicit basis of M was not constructed.

3.1 Problem 3 • Give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for A := K[x1, . . . , xn; σ]. Include an algorithm that computes a basis of a given finitely generated projective A-module.
OUTPUT: Matrices U, U−1 and a basis X of hFi, where UF U−1 = [0 0; 0 Ir] and r = dim(hFi).

accepted.question_text: Let B be a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra with finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension. Must B be a left noetherian domain? Here a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra means a connected finitely semi-graded K-algebra B with finite left global dimension d such that Ext^i_B(B/B_{≥1}, B) = 0 for i ≠ d and Ext^d_B(B/B_{≥1}, B) ≅ B/B_{≥1}.
accepted.context_brief: Noetherian-domain question for semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebras

evidence.quote: Definition 4.3. Let K be a field and B be a K-algebra. We say that B is a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra (SAS) if the following conditions hold: (i) B is a F SG ring ... (ii) B is connected ... (iii) lgld(B) := d < ∞. (iv) Exti B(B(B/B≥1),B B) ∼= 0 if i ≠ d, (B/B≥1)B if i = d.
4.3 Problem 4 • Is any SAS algebra with finite GKdim a left noetherian domain?

accepted.question_text: Let B be a semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra over a field K of characteristic 0, and assume that B is left and right noetherian, generated in degree 1, and has global dimension 3. Is B cancellative in the Zariski cancellation sense, meaning that for every K-algebra C, any isomorphism B[t] ≅ C[t] forces B ≅ C?
accepted.context_brief: Zariski cancellation for semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebras

evidence.quote: Definition 5.1 ([13]). Let R be a conmutative domain and let A be a R-algebra. (i) A is cancellative if for every R-algebra B, A[t] ∼= B[t] ⇒ A ∼= B.
5.1 Problem 5 • Let B be a SAS algebra over a field K with char(K) = 0. Assume that B is noetherian (left and right), generated in degree 1 and gld(B) = 3. Is B cancellative?
